subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored `/exec` session defaults remain authoritative after an operator changes global `tools.exec` policy, or should OpenClaw add a revocation/expiry rule for those persisted exec fields?
rationale: Current docs and tests treat `/exec` as persistent session state, but this issue shows that the same contract can keep a less restrictive exec security posture after global config is tightened.

options.title: Add explicit revocation path
options.body: Preserve documented `/exec` session defaults, but add operator-owned clearing or config-version invalidation for stored exec fields when global exec policy changes.

options.title: Make global config always win
options.body: Prioritize central policy enforcement over session defaults, accepting a compatibility break for users relying on `/exec` persistence.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave persisted session exec defaults authoritative and improve documentation or diagnostics for clearing stale session state.

recommendation.title: Add explicit revocation path
recommendation.body: Preserve documented `/exec` session defaults, but add operator-owned clearing or config-version invalidation for stored exec fields when global exec policy changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session management and exec documentation history makes this the best available owner for the product/security precedence choice.
